LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  April 13, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 5:28 p.m. on April
13, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine,
California; Mayor Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Larry Agran*
  Councilmember  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan
  *Via teleconference

Mayor Khan announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications
Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, members of the public had the ability to provide live comments on agenda
items using Zoom. Mayor Khan also assured the community that the City of Irvine was
adhering to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout City
Hall by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.

In addition, Carl Petersen, City Clerk, provided instructions on how to submit live
comments via Zoom and noted that the e-comment feature had been extended for all
agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments on
all agenda items, and would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the
City’s website.
 City Council Minutes  April 13, 2021

  Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
  not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Carroll led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Reverend Dr. Sarah Halverson-Cano from Irvine United Congregational Church provided
  the invocation.

  1.  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  1.1  Proclaim April 11-17, 2021,  as  “National  Public  Safety
  Telecommunicators Week”

  Anshul Garg, Irvine resident, spoke in support of the City Council.

  Mayor Khan presented a brief video highlighting Irvine Public Safety
  Dispatchers and issued a proclamation recognizing April 11-17, 2021, as
  “National Public Safety Telecommunicators Week.”

  Mike Hamel, Chief of Police/Director of Public Safety, provided brief
  remarks and thanked the City Council for recognizing the critical work of
  the City’s Public Safety Dispatchers.

  1.2  Proclaim April 2021 as “Arab American Heritage Month”

  Mayor Khan presented a proclamation recognizing April 2021 as “Arab
  American Heritage Month.”

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  Mayor Khan reordered the agenda to consider Presentation Item No. 2.2
  (Presentation by Team Kids) prior to Presentation Item No. 2.1 (Presentation on
  the Musick Jail Expansion).

  2.1  Presentation on the Musick Jail Expansion

  This item was considered following Presentation Item No. 2.2.

  Mayor Khan introduced Jason Park, Assistant Sheriff, Orange County
  Sheriff’s Department, who provided an update on the James A. Musick
  Jail Expansion Project.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  April 13, 2021

  City Council discussion included: questioning whether the Musick Jail
  was located on County or City land; clarified that the City does not have
  regulatory authority regarding the land use; suggested that more
  innovative solutions would create transformative and systematic change
  in how mental illness and substance use is treated; suggesting that tax
  dollars be allocated toward mental health in lieu of incarceration;
  discussed build out and per inmate costs; suggested that the City work
  with County officials to discuss concerns with the expansion project;
  noted traffic impacts to surrounding communities; inquired about the
  budget for the expansion project and how else the funds could be used if
  not expended for the project; questioned the timeline of the expansion
  project; and suggested that the Interim City Manager and City Attorney
  develop a community forum and resolution of opposition to the expansion
  project.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, clarified that the James A. Musick Jail was
  located on County land and is not subject to the City of Irvine’s land use
  authority, which limits any legal remedies the City could take regarding
  the land use. He also clarified that the City does not have land use
  authority over a governmental building unless the County pursued a
  different use.

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the proposed Musick Jail
  expansion:

  •  Terry LePage, Irvine resident
  •  Dinorah Hernandez
  •  Lulu Hammad
  •  Daisy Ramirez
  •  Ambrose Brooks
  •  Kyler Chin
  •  Margaret O’Hara
  •  Michelle M.
  •  Chelsea Boyle
  •  Karen Hernandez
  •  949-***-*689, Irvine resident
  •  Alejandro Sobrera
  •  Adam Overton
  •  Jacob Reisberg
  •  Stephen Coffey
  •  Sarah Kahn
  •  Felicity Figueroa
  •  Dave Duran
  •  Pat Davis
  •  Alex Mohajer
  •  Sylvester Ani
  •  Hanna

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  April 13, 2021

  Harvey Liss, Irvine resident, also spoke in opposition, and suggested that
  public comments be received prior to City Council discussion and
  deliberation.

  2.2  Presentation by Team Kids

  This item was considered prior to Presentation Item No. 2.1. See page 2.

  Mayor Khan introduced Julie Hudash, Founder/CEO, Team Kids, who
  provided an update on the mission, values, and planned 20th Anniversary
  activities for Team Kids.

  City Council discussion included: expressing appreciation to Ms. Hudash
  and Team Kids for its continued partnership with the City and the Irvine
  Police Department, as well as its contributions to the community;
  suggested financial support to help sponsor the Team Kids conference;
  and suggested utilization of Community Partnership Fund Grant funding
  at the discretion of each Councilmember in support of sponsoring the
  Team Kids Conference.

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to City sponsorship of the
  Team Kids Conference and expressed concern about police mentoring:

  •  Chelsea Boyle, Irvine resident
  •  Alejandro Sobrera
  •  Kyler Chin, Irvine resident
  •  Sylvester Ani Jr.
  •  Lulu Hammad, Irvine resident

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Khan, seconded by Vice Mayor Kim, to:

  Become a Founding Sponsor of the Team Kids Conference in the
  amount of $20,000, and partner with Team Kids on the four service
  projects throughout the year, which includes the September 11th
  Day of Service, the Holiday Random Acts of Kindness, the Dr.
  Martin Luther King Jr. Day of Service, and Earth Day.

  The motion carried as follows:

  AYES:  4  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Agran, Carroll, Kim
  and Khan

  NOES:  1  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Kuo

  ABSENT:  0  COUNCILMEMBERS:  None

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  April 13, 2021

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Mayor Khan wished those celebrating a Happy First Day of Ramadan; and made the
  following announcements:

  •  The City is in the process of updating its Housing Element, and the community is
  invited to attend one of two virtual meetings to learn more about this effort, and
  provide ideas and input on housing in Irvine. Irvine, along with all California cities
  and counties, is required to adequately plan for and meet the housing needs of
  everyone in the community. In the Housing Element Update, the City must identify
  enough potentially developable land suitable for residential use to meet the
  Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) allocation required by the State.
  The City’s portion of SCAG’s RHNA for the 2021-2029 Housing Element is 23,610
  units. The virtual community meetings will be held on Thursday, April 22, from 10
  a.m. to noon, and Thursday, April 29 from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. A flier with information
  on the Housing Element Update is available in eight languages, and anyone who
  needs language assistance for the community meetings can email
  mchao@cityofirvine.org by April 30 to schedule an individualized meeting. For
  information or to register (available in multiple languages), visit
  cityofirvine.org/housingelementupdate.

  •  Earth Day is April 22, and the City is offering a number of ways to celebrate all
  month long. Residents and businesses are invited to take the Restore our Earth
  Pledge and promise to complete at least seven actions that will conserve valuable
  resources and reduce pollution. To find tips for going green at work and at home,
  and to participate in online meetings and webinars, such as the Drive Electric Earth
  Day webinar on April 20 and a virtual composting class on April 23, visit
  cityofirvine.org/earthday.

  •  The community is invited to participate in the National Mayor’s Challenge for Water
  Conservation, which runs through April 30. The annual challenge to conserve
  water, sponsored by the Wyland Foundation in Irvine, reminds the City of this
  precious resource. Residents and businesses can join in this competition by
  pledging to conserve water and other resources at mywaterpledge.com. The city
  with the most pledges in each population category will win the competition, but the
  real winner in this challenge will be the planet as it is the City’s hope that this short-
  term challenge becomes a long-term practice of conservation. For more
  information, visit cityofirvine.org.

  •  The community is invited to participate in a Food Drive this Sunday from 10 a.m.
  to 12 p.m. in the Irvine City Center parking lot for Families Forward in a contactless
  drive-thru format.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  April 13, 2021

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  3.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Councilmember
  Carroll, and unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 3.1,
  3.3, 3.4, and 3.5. Consent Calendar Item No. 3.2 was removed for separate
  discussion.

  3.1  MINUTES

  ACTION:
  1) Approved the minutes of the special meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on March 9, 2021.
  2) Approved the minutes of the regular meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on March 9, 2021.

  3.2  PROCLAMATIONS

  This item was removed for separate discussion at the request of
  Councilmember Agran, who noted his support of the Armenian Genocide
  Remembrance Day proclamation, and noted minor typographical errors
  within the proclamation.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Agran,  seconded  by
  Councilmember Kuo, and unanimously carried to:

  1) Proclaim April 11-17, 2021, as "Animal Control Officer
  Appreciation Week."
  2) Proclaim April 24, 2021, as "Armenian Genocide
  Remembrance Day” as amended to correct two minor
  typographical errors.
  3) Proclaim April 2021 as "Parkinson's Awareness Month."
  4) Proclaim April 27, 2021, as "Iranian American Women's Day.”

  3.3  WARRANT AND WIRE TRANSFER RESOLUTION

  ACTION:
  Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 21-15 - A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA,
  ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND
  SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT OF WHICH THE SAME ARE
  TO BE PAID

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  6
 City Council Minutes  April 13, 2021

  3.4  NOTICE OF REVIEW FOR TRACT MAPS IN PORTOLA SPRINGS
  NEIGHBORHOOD

  ACTION:
  Receive and file.

  3.5  COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP FUND GRANT NOMINATIONS

  ACTION:
  1) Approved Councilmember Kuo's request for Community
  Partnership Fund Grant Nominations to the following
  organizations in support of program costs:

  a) Irvine Children's Fund ($1,000) (Contract No. 11302)
  b) Crime Survivor's, Inc. ($500)
  c) Families Forward ($500)
  d) Grace City Church ($250)
  e) Irvine Ranch Little League Baseball ($250)

  2) Approved Vice Mayor Kim's request for Community Partnership
  Fund Grant Nominations to Orange County Asian and Pacific
  Islander Community Alliance ($6,000) in support of Anti-Asian
  Hate initiatives. (Contract No. 11303)
  3) Authorized the Interim City Manager to prepare and sign funding
  agreements for individual awards of $1,000 or more.

  4.  COUNCIL BUSINESS

  4.1  COVID-19 SITUATIONAL UPDATE AND EXTENSION OF COVID-19
  RELATED CONTRACTS

  Michelle Grettenberg, Assistant City Manager, presented the staff report
  and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: expressing support for increasing
  vaccination efforts and utilizing the Great Park as a Super Point of
  Distribution (POD) site; and inquired about the different services offered
  between the Sand Canyon Medical Group and 360 Clinic COVID-19
  testing.

  There were no public comments.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  7
 City Council Minutes  April 13, 2021

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Khan, seconded by Councilmember Kuo,
  and unanimously carried to:

  1) Confirm the Director of Emergency Services direction to
  continue daily health screenings and contact tracing
  services for all City personnel working onsite with Sand
  Canyon Medical Group, effective April 1, 2021 through
  August 31, 2021. (Contract No. 10990F)
  2) Confirm the Director of Emergency Services direction to
  extend the contract for laboratory services with Pangea
  Laboratories, for public and employee COVID-19 testing
  through August 31, 2021. (Contract No. 11054E)

  4.2  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY MAYOR KHAN, VICE MAYOR
  KIM, AND COUNCILMEMBERS CARROLL AND KUO TO ADOPT A
  RESOLUTION AGAINST ANTI-ASIAN HATE

  This item was agendized at the request of Vice Mayor Kim, co-sponsored
  by Mayor Khan and Councilmembers Carroll and Kuo, who requested
  City Council consideration of adoption of a resolution against Anti-Asian
  hate.

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about the procedure to place
  this and other items on the agenda and potential conflicts with the Ralph
  M. Brown Act; suggested amendments to the resolution to be more
  inclusive of other communities; and reiterated that the resolution was
  written in collaboration with several community based organizations to
  highlight other communities of color that have also suffered from
  oppression.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, outlined the procedures for agendizing
  matters by multiple Councilmembers, noting that the decision to sign on
  to an agenda memo did not necessarily mean that the Councilmember
  agreed or would vote for the item on the agenda; and reiterated that
  Councilmembers have been cautioned in the past to not use the agenda
  memo process as an opportunity to deliberate.

  The following individuals spoke in support of the proposed resolution:

  •  Kyler Chin, Irvine resident
  •  Myung Suh, Irvine resident
  •  Scott Hansen, Irvine resident
  •  Naz Hamid, Irvine resident
  •  Jen Choiu, Irvine resident
  •  Kathleen Treseder, Irvine resident
  •  Chelsea Boyle, Irvine resident

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  8
 City Council Minutes  Aoril13,2021

  AGTION: Moved by Vice Mayor Kim, seconded by Councilmember
  Kuo, to:

  Adopt RESOLUTION NO. 21-16 - A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA,
  AGAINST ANTI-ASIAN HATE

  The motion carried as follows:

  AYES  4 COUNCILMEMBERS:  Carroll, Kim, Kuo
  and Khan

  NOES:  1  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Agran

  ABSENT:  0  COUNCILMEMBERS:  None

  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  The following individuals spoke in support of building the Veterans Cemetery at the

  Mitch Siegel, lrvine resident, provided a brief overview of the Orange County Hispanic

  Gail, lrvine resident, spoke in support of building the Veterans Cemetery at the ARDA

  ADJOURNMENT - IN MEMORIAM

  Prior to adjournment, Mayor Khan announced the recent passing of John Ghoukassian,

  adjourned in his memory.

  Moved by Councilmember Garroll, seconded by Vice Mayor Kim, and unanimously

  OF THE CITY OF IRVINE

  Mav 1 1,2021
  CITY CLERK OF THE CITY OF IRVINE
